result.builder:
Goal: one pull request for issue https://github.com/o/r/issues/23 that meets every one of these acceptance lines:
- math.js exports clamp(x, lo, hi), which returns x limited to the range lo to hi
- clamp(x, lo, hi) throws a RangeError when lo is greater than hi
- README.md documents every function math.js exports
- npm test passes

Current state: math.js (CommonJS, 'use strict') exports { add, subtract, multiply }. README.md has an "## API" section with "### add(a, b)" and "### multiply(a, b)" entries but NO entry for subtract. Tests live in test/math.test.js and run with `npm test` (node --test).

Steps:
1. In math.js add a function clamp(x, lo, hi) with a short doc comment, matching the existing style. If lo > hi, throw new RangeError(...) with a clear message. Otherwise return x limited to [lo, hi]: lo when x < lo, hi when x > hi, else x (bounds inclusive; lo === hi is valid and returns that value). Add clamp to module.exports, keeping add, subtract and multiply exported.
2. In README.md's "## API" section add a "### subtract(a, b)" entry (it is exported but undocumented today) and a "### clamp(x, lo, hi)" entry, each in the same style as the existing entries: a heading of the form `### name(args)`, a one-line description, and a short js example. The clamp entry must say it throws a RangeError when lo is greater than hi, and show e.g. clamp(-5, 0, 100) // 0 and clamp(140, 0, 100) // 100. Every function exported from math.js must end up with its own `### name(` heading.
3. In test/math.test.js add tests for clamp: value inside range returned unchanged, below lo returns lo, above hi returns hi, values equal to the bounds, lo === hi, and assert.throws(() => clamp(5, 10, 0), RangeError).
4. Run these and make sure all succeed before opening the PR:
   npm test
   node -e "const m=require('./math.js');const r=require('fs').readFileSync('README.md','utf8');const names=Object.keys(m).filter(k=>typeof m[k]==='function');const miss=names.filter(k=>!new RegExp('^#+\\s*'+k+'\\s*\\(','m').test(r));console.log('exports: '+names.join(', '));if(miss.length){console.log('MISSING: '+miss.join(', '));process.exit(1)}console.log('README OK')"
5. Commit and open one pull request referencing the issue.
result.verifier:
Check the PR head against issue https://github.com/o/r/issues/23. Run every command from the repository root at the PR head (run `npm install` first only if package.json now declares dependencies). Do one check per expect line, in this order, and report PASS or FAIL for each with the output you saw.

Check 1 — expect: "math.js exports clamp(x, lo, hi), which returns x limited to the range lo to hi"
Run:
node -e "const {clamp}=require('./math.js');const a=require('assert');a.strictEqual(typeof clamp,'function');a.strictEqual(clamp(5,0,10),5);a.strictEqual(clamp(-5,0,100),0);a.strictEqual(clamp(140,0,100),100);a.strictEqual(clamp(0,0,100),0);a.strictEqual(clamp(100,0,100),100);a.strictEqual(clamp(3,3,3),3);a.strictEqual(clamp(-2.5,-1.5,1.5),-1.5);console.log('CLAMP OK')"
PASS: prints CLAMP OK and exits 0. FAIL: clamp is not an exported function, or any assertion fails (non-zero exit).

Check 2 — expect: "clamp(x, lo, hi) throws a RangeError when lo is greater than hi"
Run:
node -e "const {clamp}=require('./math.js');const a=require('assert');a.throws(()=>clamp(5,10,0),RangeError);a.throws(()=>clamp(0,1,0.5),RangeError);console.log('RANGE OK')"
PASS: prints RANGE OK and exits 0. FAIL: either call does not throw, or throws something that is not a RangeError (non-zero exit).

Check 3 — expect: "README.md documents every function math.js exports"
Run:
node -e "const m=require('./math.js');const r=require('fs').readFileSync('README.md','utf8');const names=Object.keys(m).filter(k=>typeof m[k]==='function');const miss=names.filter(k=>!new RegExp('^#+\\s*'+k+'\\s*\\(','m').test(r));console.log('exports: '+names.join(', '));if(miss.length){console.log('MISSING: '+miss.join(', '));process.exit(1)}console.log('README OK')"
Then open README.md and read the entry for each listed export (note: subtract was undocumented before this change, so it must now be covered too).
PASS: every exported function listed has a README entry that describes what it does (the script prints README OK; if it prints MISSING for a name that README.md does document under a differently formatted heading or text, read it and judge by whether that function is actually documented). FAIL: any exported function has no description in README.md.

Check 4 — expect: "npm test passes"
Run: npm test
PASS: exits 0 with fail 0. FAIL: non-zero exit or any failing test.

Advisory (does not affect PASS/FAIL):
- Whether test/math.test.js adds tests for clamp, including the RangeError case.
- Whether clamp(2,2,2) (lo === hi) returns 2 without throwing.
- Whether the README clamp entry mentions the RangeError.
